additions: H1: Visual Studio Code 1.146
Release date: November 11, 2026 Stable
H2: Downloads for 1.146.0

Save your brainpower for the work that needs it. Inbox mode keeps the right sessions on your radar while agents take on model comparisons. Shape your agent workspace around the task with chat windows and extensions.
Inbox mode (Experimental): Focus on sessions that need your attention across all your projects, and snooze others for later.
Model comparison (Preview): Compare results with Copilot Fusion in the mix, or let an agent run comparisons for you.
Chat windows (Preview): Give chats their own windows and rearrange chats, editors, and terminals to fit the task.
Extensions in the Agents window (Experimental): Find and install extensions for a richer agent experience.
Local harness deprecation: Move to the Copilot harness before the Local harness is removed in February 2027.
Happy coding!
H2: Agents
H3: Copilot harness and deprecation of the Local harness

The Copilot harness is our latest agent harness and has been the default for new sessions since VS Code 1.143. It's built on the Copilot SDK, a shared foundation that helps align behavior, capabilities, and improvements across Copilot products. Copilot harness sessions run through the Agent Host, so you can keep them running in the background and access them from both the VS Code editor window and the Agents window. For organizations, the Copilot harness also enforces managed sandbox and permission policies that the Local harness doesn't.

Thank you to everyone who has shared feedback on using the Copilot harness as your default. Your feedback has shaped the harness experience, and it will continue to guide us through this next step. As of this release, the Local harness is deprecated and will be removed in three months (February 2027):

Next three months: You can still use the Local harness while you move your workflows, but it's functionally frozen. New features and improvements will focus on the Copilot harness and are not guaranteed to be supported by the Local harness.

additions: To start a session in the background without navigating into it, press Alt+Enter or hold Alt and select Send. Focus stays in the composer so you can start another task. Select Open Session in the confirmation to open the sent conversation. With the Inbox mode setting enabled, you can also press Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS).

Confirm the active session before sending feedback or running commands. For steering and stopping requests, see Use chat. To group, pin, or prioritize sessions that need attention, see Organize and triage sessions.
H3: Open chats in separate windows
To keep a conversation and its files on another display, enable
sessions.chatWindows.enabled
Open in VS Code
Open in VS Code Insiders
, then right-click a session or chat in the sessions list and select Open in > New Window. The setting is on by default in Insiders.
You can also drag a chat tab or session title out of the window to open it separately, or into another chat window to move it there.

Use Configure Layout in the new window's title bar to show chat and editors side by side or stacked. In the stacked layout, run Agents: Toggle Chat Conversation from the Command Palette to hide the conversation and keep only the input visible.

To rearrange content, hover over the top edge of a chat, editor, or terminal area to reveal its layout handle. Drag the handle to an edge of another area, using the placement preview to choose its new position.
To move the window's chats and editors back to the main window, select More Actions (...) > Move to Main Window in the chat header.
